turns.user: Do I need a Mexican fishing license for a 1.5 day trip?
turns.text:
Short answer: if the trip fishes in Mexican waters, yes — you'll need a Mexican sport-fishing permit (CONAPESCA) and to be on the boat's FMM passenger list, with your passport. If it stays in US waters, no.

From the regulations summary (last checked 2026-11-25):
- **Mexican sport-fishing permit** (CONAPESCA) is required to fish from a boat in Mexican waters. Sold by day/week/month/year/excursion. [CONAPESCA](https://www.gob.mx/conapesca/documentos/conapesca-01-016-pesca-deportivo-recreativa)
- Foreigners entering Mexican waters by boat must be on the boat's **INM passenger list (FMM)** with the immigration fee paid. **Carry your passport.** [INM](https://www.gob.mx/inm/acciones-y-programas/sport-fishing-and-nautical-tourism)

The data doesn't tell me which specific 1.5-day trips cross into Mexican waters, so confirm with the landing. Most 1.5-day listings I have note "MX permit extra" — for example, the **Tribute** (Seaforth), **Constitution** (Fisherman's, "passport not required"), and **Old Glory** (H&M) list it. Always confirm the exact docs on the landing's site before booking.
